signals.entity: Ministrstvo za finance / Banka Slovenije (ZDUPS bill)
signals.signal: NEW second public draft of the Zakon o dostopnosti in uporabi placilnih sredstev (ZDUPS - Law on Accessibility and Use of Payment Means) published 17/07/2026, consultation open to 17/08/2026 (13/08/2026 for municipalities via ZMOS). Draft mandates: at least 60 ATMs per 100,000 inhabitants nationally; an ATM within 5 km of the centre of every settlement above 1,000 residents; a bank branch or Post Office banking point within 5 km for settlements above 3,000 residents; at least 40 branches per 100,000 inhabitants; 95% of residents within 5 km road distance of cash; max 3% of the ATM requirement substitutable by cash-in-shop/cashback points; five free withdrawals OR DEPOSITS per month at any bank's ATM; and merchants must accept euro cash AND offer at least one electronic payment method (exemptions: turnover under EUR 10,000, first-year start-ups, charity, no safe connectivity). Government timetable on the e-Demokracija register (evidenca 2026-1611-0028, Ministrstvo za finance): adoption and entry into force targeted Q4-2026. Plain language: a cash-access law that legally forces banks to run a minimum ATM and branch estate, and forces shops to take cards.
signals.source_name: e-Uprava / e-Demokracija - Predlog predpisa: Zakon o dostopnosti in uporabi placilnih sredstev (id 18855) + ZMOS bill page (jul 26)
signals.implies: Direct, sizeable ATM-deployment and cash-automation opportunity: banks that have been thinning their networks will have to re-deploy machines into low-density settlements. Free DEPOSITS at ATMs pushes banks toward deposit-capable and recycling machines (NCR intelligent-deposit / recyclers, Glory-Sesami TCRs) rather than dispense-only, plus x-core multivendor ATM software, ATM telemetry/monitoring, cash optimisation (NCR APTRA OptiCash) to run a bigger, less profitable estate economically, physical ATM security for unmanned rural sites, and managed/field services for a geographically dispersed fleet. The merchant e-payment obligation is a POS/softPOS acceptance opportunity for acquirers.
signals.likelihood: High - bill is on the Government's own Q4-2026 adoption timetable and has Banka Slovenije co-authorship; banks will need supplier commitments before the law bites
signals.followup: Download the ZDUPS draft PDF from the e-Demokracija entry and extract the transition period (how long banks get to comply) and any penalty regime; then map the gap between the current Slovenian ATM estate and 60/100k + the 1,000-resident rule per bank (NLB, OTP SI, Nova KBM/OTP, SKB, Sparkasse, Delavska hranilnica, Gorenjska banka, Addiko SI, Intesa SI) and build a per-bank shortfall pitch.

signals.entity: Lider.si / ZDUPS impact - Slovenian ATM density baseline
signals.signal: Slovenia currently has 61.1 ATMs per 100,000 inhabitants against the draft ZDUPS requirement of 60 per 100,000 - i.e. the national aggregate is only marginally above the proposed floor, so the binding constraint is the GEOGRAPHIC rule (an ATM within 5 km of every settlement over 1,000 residents and 95% population coverage), not the headline count. Any further network rationalisation would immediately breach the floor.
signals.source_name: Lider.si - 'Slovenija ima 61,1 bankomata na 100.000 prebivalcev, novi predlog jih zahteva 60'
signals.implies: The compliance gap is about WHERE machines sit, not how many exist in total - which favours redeployment/relocation projects, off-branch and through-the-wall installs with physical ATM security, and remote monitoring/managed services for isolated units, rather than a pure volume ATM tender.
signals.likelihood: High that geographic redeployment becomes the 2027 workstream at every Slovenian bank
signals.followup: Verify the 61.1/100k figure against Banka Slovenije payment-statistics (bsi.si) and the ECB Payments Statistics (SDW), then produce a settlement-level coverage heat map for Slovenia to identify the specific under-served settlements.
